title: An Extremely Young Protostellar Core, MMS 1/OMC-3: Episodic Mass Ejection History Traced by the Micro SiO Jet
question: Does the OMC-3 source MMS 1 host a protostar, and what do its compact CO outflow and SiO jet reveal about its age and episodic mass ejection history?

data.angular_resolution: CO 0.18x0.15 arcsec, SiO 0.21x0.17 arcsec, continuum 0.19x0.16 arcsec (high res)
data.sensitivity: continuum rms 0.24 mJy/beam (high res); CO 2.7, SiO 1.8 mJy/beam km/s in 5 km/s channels

what.value: Inclination of 45 deg from dust-disk axis ratio, used for dynamical timescales

evidence.quote: Here, we adopt $i=45^{\circ}$, estimated from the axis ratio of the dust disk by (cite: Liu2023).
${\kappa}_{\rm{1.3mm}}$ = 0.011 cm$^2$ g$^{-1}$ from the dust coagulation model of the MRN (cite: mathis1977) with thin ice mantles at a number density of 10$^{8}$ cm$^{-3}$ (cite: ossenkopf1994)
d$ = 393 pc (distance to the OMC-3 region measured from the $Gaia$ DR2 data; (cite: Tobin2020; McBride2019; Gaia2018))

what.value: JCMT 850 um light curve of MMS 1 and flux calibration uncertainty <2%

evidence.quote: For bright sources, such as MMS 1, the relative flux calibration uncertainty between epochs is better than 2% (cite: Mairs2017).

recipe.method: tclean with Briggs weighting on high- and low-resolution data; compare line flux between them to check missing flux

recipe.goal: Fit continuum structure and estimate disk mass
recipe.method: Two-component 2D Gaussian fit to high-resolution continuum; mass from optically thin dust emission equation
assumptions: Gas-to-dust mass ratio of 100; thermal dust emission dominates; compact component traces disk with inclination from axis ratio

recipe.goal: Measure outflow and jet morphology, PV diagrams, velocities
recipe.method: Moment maps and PV diagram cut along outflow axis p.a. = -137 deg from CO and SiO cubes
t_dyn = (l_obs/v_obs)(cos i / sin i) for jet, outflow and knots
assumptions: Outflow extends to the bow-shock locations

recipe.method: 3D spiral parametric model fit by eye to northern and southern jets separately

recipe.goal: Compare PV diagram with MHD simulation and JCMT light curve
recipe.method: Qualitative comparison with Machida & Basu 2019 PV diagrams; inspect 850 um light curve for bursts

answer_key.quantity: Disk inclination from compact axis ratio

evidence.quote: an inclination angle of the disk ($i$) is estimated to be ${\sim}53^{\circ}$ using the axis ratio
the jet dynamical timescale is estimated to be 66 yr (blue-shifted jet) and 55 yr (red-shifted jet), respectively.
the outflow dynamical timescales are estimated to be 350 yr (blue-shifted side) and 660 yr (red-shifted side), respectively.

evidence.loc: 3.4.2 Dynamical Timescale to Each SiO Knot
evidence.quote: which are 5 yr (K1), 18 yr (K2), 45 yr (K3), and 53 yr (K4)
There is, however, a distinct $\sim$ 0.5% per year gradual decline in the brightness

not_stated_but_needed: Exact line-free channel ranges for continuum and any continuum subtraction method
Image size, cell size, masking, clean threshold and deconvolver for tclean
Method for deriving PV-diagram cuts, moment-map thresholds and knot positions/velocities
Bandpass/flux standard model and flux density values for calibrators
score_reason: Basic imaging parameters given and data archival, but moment/PV extraction and many settings unstated; precession fit by eye.
rediscovery_reason: Data from a single ALMA project; numeric results (Gaussian fits, timescales) can be redone with stated recipe.
